newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Chechen leader meet over peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Chechen leader meet over peace deal.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov started a meeting on Monday which may result in the signing of a political accord aimed at turning last year's ceasefire into a lasting peace.

"We are here to remove all remaining differences and sign the peace treaty," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying before going into the one-on-one Kremlin meeting with Maskhadov at around noon (0800 GMT).

"I have come here with peace and in the name of peace," Interfax quoted Maskhadov as saying as he arrived in Moscow. "The war is ending, for the first time in the history of relations between Moscow and Grozny, and the era of peace is starting."
Tens of thousands of people died in an ill-fated Russian military operation to crush Chechnya's independence drive which began in December 1994 and stopped last August after a ceasefire.

No details of the draft agreement have been made public and the date of Maskhadov's visit had been kept secret. Negotiators on both sides said they had done all they could and it was up to the two leaders to remove remaining differences.
